name: zlib-c
algorithm: Compress a text file into a zlib stream (RFC 1950) at level 6 with each language's library, reading the input in 64 KiB chunks and writing the output file; the check is a round trip through Go's compress/zlib (README.md).

c.name: zlib
c.inside: none (the portable C of adler32.c, crc32.c, deflate.c, trees.c, zutil.c and the inflate files; no assembly, no intrinsics)

rust.name: flate2
rust.inside: its default rust_backend: miniz_oxide 0.8.8 and adler2 2.0.0, which forbid unsafe code; crc32fast 1.4.2, linked, has unsafe SIMD (pclmulqdq) for gzip's CRC-32, which the zlib framing does not run; flate2's own unsafe code is in its C backends, not enabled

notes: The input is the wordfreq row's text (tools/bench gen kind words, seed 3, bytes 50,000,000; the generator writes whole words until it reaches the size, then a newline, here 50,000,001 bytes; the same file). The size is provisional: verify -publish-size in the coordinator's window fixes it. idiomatic/wordfreq reads this file under the same spec, so a new size for this row needs a new file name (for example wordfreq-<size>.txt), or the two rows would name two specs for one file.

Level 6 in every cell: zlib's and flate2's default and what Go's DefaultCompression (-1) selects, Zig's Options.default (level_6), and Mk's Encoder takes the level explicitly. The compressed bytes differ by library, so they are never compared; their size is printed beside each cell.
C: zlib 1.3.1 from Mk-evidence/vendor (D-588), compiled with the C column's flags. Rust: flate2 1.1.1 from a cargo vendor tree in Mk-evidence (crates), by directory source replacement (D-835).
